land.text: the Transcaspian Oblast, held by the Tashkent Soviet until the revolt of July 1918

predecessors.note: The Turkestan Soviet Federative Republic had been proclaimed on 30 April 1918.

land.text: regained by the Tashkent Soviet by 1920

successors.note: TG: the lead says the government lasted to July 1919, the infobox to February 1920.

capitals.name: Ashgabat (Ashkhabad)
capitals.note: TG: 'Capital: Ashgabat'; 'based at Ashgabat, Transcaspian Oblast'.

correction.text: 'based at Ashgabat, Transcaspian Oblast' (TG); the page names no other town as held, and gives no area

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, no Cliopatria row: the Transcaspian Oblast as a floor (Ahal, Balkan, Mary admin-1s, about 269,000 km2). Merv and Chardzhou are not on the page; the front lines are unknown.

ledger.note: 1918: Ashgabat rises against the Tashkent Bolsheviks. Infobox 'Established: 12 July 1918'; 'On 14 July 1918 The Ashkhabad Executive Committee was founded' by Mensheviks and Social Revolutionaries 'following their successful revolt against the Bolsheviks of Tashkent'.

1918: the committee becomes the Trans Caspian Provisional Government. 'This committee took the name of the Trans Caspian Provisional Government in November 1918'; on 20 September 1918 it executed the 26 Baku Commissars.

1920: the Bolsheviks retake Transcaspia. After the British withdrew, 'the Bolsheviks went on the offensive and defeated the Transcaspian forces'; 'By 1920 the Tashkent Soviet had regained control of the area'; infobox 'Disestablished: February 1920' (the lead says July 1919).

wars.name: Transcaspian campaign (Malleson mission)
wars.outcome: The Ashkhabad government, helped by the Anglo-Indian Malleson mission, held Transcaspia until the British withdrew; by 1920 the Tashkent Soviet had regained it.
wars.note: Dates: TG's lead says 1918 to July 1919, its infobox February 1920.

certainty.note: A rebel regime on the railway line from Krasnovodsk to Ashgabat; no frontier is described.

sources.title: Transcaspian Government
sources.note: Established 12 July 1918; the Ashkhabad Executive Committee 14 July; renamed November 1918; the 26 Baku Commissars; Malleson mission; disestablished February 1920.

notes: Written for batch ia-03-x from one page (TG, budget 1-2). The page gives no area and no towns beyond Ashgabat and Krasnovodsk (where the Baku Commissars fled); TG's own dates disagree (lead 1918 to July 1919, infobox February 1920, followed). The British forces are not recorded as an occupation: the page says only that a Malleson mission unit and a machine-gun team came.
